answer: No. Your records show you did not have a blood clot in your lung. On July 8, 2025 you had a CT scan of the chest with contrast, done to look for one. It was read as: no pulmonary embolism, lungs clear, no fluid around the lungs or heart, and only mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of the upper back. A blood test that evening (D-dimer) was mildly high at 0.92, but that test is often high for reasons that have nothing to do with clots, and the scan answered the question. A 'pulmonary embolism' entry exists from that day, but it is marked as refuted and resolved, meaning it was ruled out. The diagnosis that stood was chest wall pain, which was listed as resolved by July 22, 2025. I found no later record of a lung clot or of any blood thinner. If you have new chest pain, breathlessness or leg swelling, tell a clinician promptly.
short: A chest CT angiogram on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism; the PE diagnosis was recorded as refuted, and chest wall pain was the confirmed diagnosis.
